question.text: Without changing the direction of the axes, the origin is transferred to the point (2,3) . Then the equation $x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x-6 y+9=0$ changes to

solution.text:
Put 
$x=x^{\prime}+2$
and $\quad y=y^{\prime}+3$
$\therefore \quad x^{2}+y^{2}-4 x-6 y+9=0$
$$
\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \quad\left(x^{\prime}+2\right)^{2}+\left(y^{\prime}+3\right)^{2}-4\left(x^{\prime}+2\right) \\
-6(y+3)+9=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+4+4 x^{2}+y^{2}+9 \\
\quad+6 y^{\prime}-4 x^{2}-8-6 y^{\prime}-18+9=0 \\
\Rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-4=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad x^{2}+y^{2}=4
\end{array}
$$
